Although we're not fat, we don't often eat right. Any tips other than the basics to easy right on a really tight budget?

Yeah - starve.

J/K, but seriously - a lot of people tend to eat when they are bored and are raised eating at appropriate meal times, not necessarily when they are hungry. People don't actually understand 'hungry' anymore - there is full, 'not hungry, but I could eat', and that horrible pain in your stomach when you need to eat something RIGHT NOW or you are going to get sick. It is very hard to relearn how to know when to eat.

Some tips I've found help eating right on a budget: stock up on rice (any kind - it doesn't matter. Rice is filling and you can eat less of it. People will say 'but brown rice is better for you' - it tastes like butt, especially if you are used to eating high-salt high-fat foods. If you don't want to eat it you have just wasted your money, so why bother. Charge start small - buy white rice.) Portion that shit and remember to wait 20 MINUTES after eating it to decide if you want a second helping. Is your stomach gurgling for more food? No? You have completed a feeding. I know you are bored and think you want more - go find something to do for, like, two hours. It's a like a cigarette craving - it will pass.

Invest in broth base/bouillon - comes in a big jar or boxes with little squares in it ('that is so high in sodium' yes, and your body needs it if you are cutting down on the food you eat. Don't be scared. It looks like you need a mom to prepare it but it's super easy.) Cook your rice in broth and it makes it tasty, especially if you are eating rice a lot. Also, makes good soup. Wanna go all hippie on it and get free range, blessed by sri lanken monks, and made beside Lake Minnetonka bouillon? Go for it - but you don't really need to. The extra stuff is negligible.

Go to a butcher. Seriously. And buy your meat in bulk. Set side, like, 30-60 bucks a month and just go buy a bulk package of beef or pork or chicken. 10 lb bag of ground hamburger. It will save you so much money. Real butchers harvest their own meat gardens and real meat doesn't last very long. A good butcher knows this and won't sell meat that is going to turn brown on you that night like wal mart and most chain grocery stores will. They also tend to sell their meat extra lean or trimmed for friggin pennies. My butcher never has ground beef with more than 85 percent fat - the fattier stuff is sold to the grocery store. And his stuff costs less. 3.49 a lb for 85% at the store, 2.13/lb for extra lean ground beef at the butcher. I shape mine into hamburgers and freeze them. And is fucking amazing. You will be surprised how little meat you actually need when half of it doesn't melt away when you are cooking it.

Last thing, probably the biggest pain in the ass - make cooking a meal 'a thing'. Like for you and whoever you live with. Bring the laptop into the kitchen and turn on South Park or Rick and Morty (i assume there are other shows people watch together out there, i just don't know what they are.). Each take a part to cook - one does the main dish maybe and one does a side or something. Food tastes better when someone else makes it. This will help you both (or more) eat better because those carrot you kinda 'meh' when you cook will taste great when someone else made them. You kind of trick each other into eating better and only eating when both of you are preparing food. It also tricks you into wanting to prepare more instead of instant-fooding everything. You'll want the prep to last through the show or through the conversation, so you make more complicated meals, which involve ingredients with more prep, blah blah blah.

You can ENJOY food, and please do - I'm not suggesting you only eat rice and bouillon. But if you eat cake every friggin' day you are going to be unhealthy. Potato chips for every meal? Not healthy. Potato chips with one meal a day? Not going to kill you, just watch you portion size. Just learn when you are hungry and when you are full, that's really the hardest part.
